title: An expression can feed back into the feelings
summary: OpenStax describes the facial feedback hypothesis as the idea that a facial expression can influence the feelings, including that smiling can make a person feel happier.
body: OpenStax Psychology states the facial feedback hypothesis as the claim that facial expressions can influence feelings, so smiling can make a person feel happier. The page points to studies for that idea and then reports a Botox finding: depressed people reported less depression after frowning muscles were paralyzed. Those studies were not opened here. The sentence is the textbook's account, not a promise that forcing a grin will change how a particular person feels.

sources.title: 10.4 Emotion

sources.note: Supports the facial-feedback paragraph and the Botox frowning-muscle sentence as OpenStax reports it. OpenStax Psychology, first edition (publish date 2014-12-08), CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase of the opened page; the cited primary paper was not opened.
